November 15, 2026

Iran strikes US base in Bahrain with drones

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

Bahrain's military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks on Sunday, its first interceptions since September, and accused Iran of a systematic hostile approach toward the kingdom. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said six drones targeted US radar at Bahrain's Al-Rifaa helicopter base in response to hostile US actions. Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Talks have not produced a deal to end the war, which began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

Cabinet officials moved to military bases over reported Iranian drone plot

tags: defence, politics, war
sources: @ericmoutsos

Israeli intelligence reportedly warned the CIA of an Iranian plot to target President Donald Trump and senior US officials with explosive-laden drones. Several cabinet members, including Scott Bessent, Stephen Miller and Marco Rubio, have been moved from their homes to military bases, and Trump is said to be remaining at the White House. The warning cited specific recent threats involving drone swarms that could overwhelm domestic defences. There has been no independent confirmation of the intelligence.

Nationwide ground stop after FAA communications outage cancels thousands of flights

tags: politics, tech
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

A communications failure prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to halt departures across the United States for hours on Friday, with knock-on delays in Canada. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage began during a contractor's upgrade from copper wiring to fibre-optic cable, and that a router replacement in El Dorado, Arkansas triggered a Texas router to flood other centres with data; about 60 similar routers have been disabled and there is no evidence of a cyberattack. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford estimated 4,000 to 5,000 cancellations on Saturday, and Sunday brought a further 1,924, for a three-day total of 17,822. Duffy said operations should be fully normal Monday and is seeking $50 billion for system upgrades.

Trump blames Biden for air traffic failure as officials refuse to apologise

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Roughly 24 hours after the nationwide ground stop, Trump made his first comments, attributing the failure to the Biden administration and calling the air traffic system 50 years old while demanding that Congress quickly approve billions of dollars for upgrades. Sean Duffy likewise said the administration would not apologise, placing responsibility on the previous administration, even as officials acknowledged the system was being upgraded when it crashed. House Speaker Mike Johnson blamed Democrats for not supporting additional FAA funding, though Republicans hold the House, Senate and White House and passed large funding increases for ICE and CBP without Democratic votes. During the disruption Trump also posted about his golf course and circulated AI-generated images depicting himself in the Oval Office.

Trump to hold first trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin

tags: politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

The White House confirmed that Trump will meet China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, in their first three-way sit-down. A senior US official said the meeting could open nuclear arms talks among the three countries, that no deals were expected, and that Trump planned to discuss the war with Iran while avoiding Ukraine. Trump wants China included in a nuclear pact after New START expired in February, ending limits on the US and Russian arsenals. Pentagon estimates put China's stockpile at more than 600 warheads, against more than 5,000 each for Russia and the United States.

White House threatens criminal prosecution of Senator Elizabeth Warren

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A US attorney in Texas sent Senator Elizabeth Warren a letter demanding she preserve documents related to her investigations of corporations that associate closely with Trump. White House chief of staff Stephen Miller reposted the letter alongside references to 18 U.S.C. 241 and 242, federal conspiracy statutes covering deprivation of rights under colour of law. The move amounts to a threat to prosecute a sitting senator over congressional investigations. The Constitution's speech or debate clause protects legislative functions, including investigations, from criminal prosecution.

Republican senators block Trump judicial nominees from their states

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina are blocking several of Trump's judicial nominees from their home states. The White House is trying to confirm lifetime federal appointments quickly before Democrats take control of the Senate with an expected 56 seats. The two senators say they will slow-walk the process rather than grant blanket approval, which would reduce the number of judges confirmed.

Senate nears vote on permitting bill that would fast-track data centers and gas plants

tags: climate, politics, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

The Senate could hold a final vote this week on BAAJA, a permitting bill co-written by Utah Senator Mike Lee, which would speed approvals for gas pipelines, gas-fired power plants and the data centers that draw on them. The bill would give communities as little as 150 days to challenge a project in court. Tribal leaders and several senators warn it would weaken protections for sacred and cultural sites. Opponents argue the decision should be left to the Congress elected this month, which takes office in January, and are urging senators to vote no and to back an amendment protecting tribal sacred sites.

Defense secretary says international law should not bind US military

tags: defence, legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States military should not be bound by international law, telling critics to stop quoting laws to men with swords. The remarks responded to Secretary of State Marco Rubio's comments about the International Criminal Court and its work holding war criminals accountable. The exchange follows a US strike in Iran that killed more than a hundred people, including children at a girls' school.

Whistleblower says warnings about air defence at Kuwait port were ignored

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Army Major Stephen Ramsbottom has filed a whistleblower complaint alleging that commanders ignored warnings about aerial protection at Port Shuaiba, Kuwait. An Iranian drone killed six US soldiers at the site on March 1. Ramsbottom described the incident as a tactical failure. The Pentagon declined to comment.

Iran says supertanker sank after mine strikes in Strait of Hormuz

tags: war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck mines on an unauthorised route in the southern Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, and that one, a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude, sank in the Gulf. The Guards did not name the vessels and there was no independent confirmation. The US military says it has cleared the main shipping routes of mines.

Administration rolls back passenger protections as stranded travelers face surge pricing

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Over the past 18 months the administration has rolled back airline passenger rules covering cash compensation, wheelchair handling and hidden fees, according to reporting cited in the posts. This year it abandoned a Biden-era rule requiring airlines to disclose charges for extras and undid a 15-year-old requirement that final ticket prices be displayed prominently, while largely halting fines against carriers. Travelers stranded by the ground stop are meanwhile facing surge pricing from ride-hailing and rental car companies, prompting calls for price-gouging enforcement.

Alaska elects first Democratic governor since 1998

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, won Alaska's race for governor, defeating three Republicans including a candidate backed by Trump. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski backed Kreiss-Tomkins. The result brings Democrats to 30 governorships after midterm gains in states including Georgia and Texas. Kreiss-Tomkins campaigned on household costs and full funding for public schools and said he wanted Republicans, Democrats and independents in his cabinet.

Texas Democrats move to reverse Republican policies after midterm wins

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Following sweeping victories in Texas, Democrats have begun introducing legislation to undo Republican measures, including the required display of the Ten Commandments in public schools. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has made a statewide teacher pay raise a priority. Democrats also plan to roll back the state's observance of Confederate Heroes Day each January.

Congressional scrutiny sought over Trump ally and alleged Chinese spy

tags: politics, surveillance
sources: @carolinegleich

A close ally of Trump was reported to have been in a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, and Trump was said to have known about it and taken the ally on a trip to Beijing. The post calls for a congressional investigation. It contrasts that case with accusations that Utah residents questioning a local data center project were acting as Chinese proxies.

Dark money flows from political action committees to online creators

tags: politics, media
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Federal Election Commission filings show Haley Stevens for Senate received $30.6 million from AIPAC during the 2025-2026 cycle and disbursed $10,000 in October 2025 to Good Influence, a for-profit creator marketing firm, for social media consulting. Good Influence shares a founder, Stuart Perilmuter, with Chorus, a 501(c)(4) non-profit co-founded with Brian Tyler Cohen whose funding cannot be traced. Chorus says it has roughly 200 creators, who are not required to disclose their membership or that content is paid. The posts call for legislation requiring creators to disclose paid political content, and note that one creator said he received $24,000 from the Chorus program in early 2025.

Louisiana to castrate former officer sentenced for child sex crimes

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Cajun Williams, a 31-year-old former police officer in Louisiana, was sentenced to three life terms after conviction on charges including first-degree rape and indecent behaviour with a juvenile. As part of the punishment he will also be castrated. Louisiana became the first state in 2024 to permit castration as a sentence for certain sex crimes, and this is believed to be among the first applications of that law. It is not clear whether the castration will be surgical or chemical.

Kentucky county magistrate race decided by coin toss

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Democrat Kristen Gifford Fryman won the District 2 magistrate seat in Robertson County, Kentucky, by coin toss after she and Republican Benny Ray Renner each received 91 votes. The state election board recommended the tiebreaker, Kentucky's third of the year. Fryman will join the fiscal court, which sets the county budget and tax rates.
